summary:
A bounded synthetic local fake-provider observation of Codex0.166.0 emitted one request with no top-level tools property but an input additional_tools block carrying runtime tool definitions, automatic tool choice and injected developer/environment context despite discovered tool switches being disabled. No real provider or model ran. This demonstrates an isolation failure for that tested configuration; it does not prove every configuration fails. Read-only sandboxing, fresh conversations and tool flags alone cannot establish outcome-blinded context.

The source boundary verifies sealed task/manifests/Git blobs, flattens a predeclared bounded context plan, rejects tool/control frames and injected request context, and keeps responses ineligible with effective profile Unknown. Leaf reads must open nonblocking before checking regular-file status; otherwise a no-writer FIFO hangs before byte limits. Actual inference launch remains refused: no qualified canonical data-only transport or existing approved API credential was established. Source/control success is not a hardness predictor, cross-profile invariance or installed adoption. The wider #5276/#5248 acceptance remains open.
title: Codex tool absence must be checked inside actual request inputs
